OHUYDjP9DVQ.title: Toyota Cheated So Well, the FIA Called It Genius
OHUYDjP9DVQ.description:
How Toyota Team Europe hid an illegal turbo restrictor in the 1995 World Rally Championship, in the Celica GT-Four ST205, and why FIA president Max Mosley called it genius.
Toyota was leading both world championships with two rallies left. Then scrutineers at Rally Catalunya took Auriol's car apart.

Which side are you on: genius, or just cheating? Tell us in the comments.

YPdVXp1ca0c.title: Ferrari vs Lamborghini: The Insult That Started It All
YPdVXp1ca0c.description:
Ferruccio Lamborghini was a tractor maker who drove Ferraris. When the clutch kept failing, he went to Maranello to complain, and Enzo Ferrari supposedly told him he'd never handle a Ferrari. This is the full Lamborghini vs Ferrari origin story.

He built a V12 rival in four months, showed a car with no engine, then shocked the world with the Miura, the car that invented the supercar. Was the insult real, or a story Ferruccio liked to tell? And who actually won: Ferrari or Lamborghini?

u6lgliMatSk.title: Porsche Bought a Nissan to Prove It Cheated. It Backfired.
u6lgliMatSk.description:
In 2008 Porsche bought a Nissan GT-R, flew it to Germany, lapped the Nürburgring and accused Nissan of cheating with race tyres. Nissan's reply: maybe Porsche's drivers needed lessons. This is the full GT-R vs Porsche 911 Turbo story.

The R35 Nissan GT-R cost about half the price of a Porsche 911 Turbo, yet Nissan claimed a 7:29 Nordschleife lap, faster than Porsche's own GT2. Porsche's test came back at 7:54. Here's what Porsche said, what Nissan answered, and how Godzilla kept getting faster, all the way to the GT-R Nismo's 7:08.

NJSd2W415nA.title: Toyota Lost Money on Every Lexus LFA. Owners Didn't.
NJSd2W415nA.description:
In 2010, Toyota sold the Lexus LFA for $375,000 and still lost money on every single one. Today one has sold for $1.81 million. Here's the full story of Toyota's craziest supercar.

The 4.8-litre V10 built with Yamaha revved from idle to 9,000 rpm in 0.6 seconds, so fast that a needle couldn't keep up and Lexus fitted a digital rev counter. Toyota threw away five years of work on an aluminium car and started again in carbon fibre, tuned the engine's sound like a musical instrument, chased the Nürburgring, and built only 500 cars by hand.

LjII0wBnJHA.title: Why Ferrari FEARED This Honda | Honda NSX Story
LjII0wBnJHA.description:
The full Honda NSX (Acura NSX) history: how Ayrton Senna called Honda's secret supercar "fragile" at Suzuka in 1989, and how Honda answered with an aluminium body, a VTEC V6 and a chassis 50% stiffer, the car that woke up Ferrari.

From the 1984 Pininfarina HP-X concept and the NS-X reveal at the 1989 Chicago Auto Show, to Senna's test, eight more months of Nürburgring development with Motoharu Kurosawa, the 3.0-litre C30A V6 with titanium connecting rods revving to 8,000 rpm, the hand-built cars from Tochigi, and what a $60,000 Acura NSX is worth today, this is the full NSX story.

flQ66uxn0DM.title: The AE86 Wasn't Fast. So Why Is It a Legend?
flQ66uxn0DM.description:
The full Toyota AE86 history: how a slow, cheap 1983 Corolla became the Hachi-Roku legend behind Initial D and drifting. It was never fast, so why does everyone still want one?

R9jLpyg8-3A.title: Mazda's Rotary Engine Should Never Have Worked (RX-7 & 787B Story)
R9jLpyg8-3A.description:
The Mazda rotary engine has no pistons. It drinks fuel, burns oil, and nearly bankrupted Mazda, yet it won Le Mans with the 787B and powered the RX-7. So why do people love the rotary so much?

_QTVeqC9ARM.title: Why the Nissan Skyline GT-R R34 Was Banned in America (Godzilla's Full Story)
_QTVeqC9ARM.description:
Why was the Nissan Skyline GT-R R34 banned in the USA, and is the R34 finally legal to import in 2026? For 25 years Americans could only drive Godzilla in Gran Turismo. This is the complete R34 GT-R history: from the 1969 Hakosuka to the R32 that earned the "Godzilla" nickname, the RB26DETT twin-turbo engine, the 25-year import rule and the $1.357 million Paul Walker R34 auction.

In this episode of Piston Origins:
- Where the GT-R name began (1969 Skyline 2000GT-R "Hakosuka", PGC10)
- How the R32 GT-R got the name Godzilla (Wheels magazine, Australia)
- The R34 GT-R reveal (January 8, 1999): shorter, stiffer, sharper
- RB26DETT: 2.6L inline-six, twin turbos, 276 hp "gentlemen's agreement"
- ATTESA E-TS Pro AWD, Super-HICAS, Getrag 6-speed and the 5.8" MFD screen
- Why the R34 was illegal in the US (FMVSS, the Motorex import loophole)
- Gran Turismo, 2 Fast 2 Furious and the JDM generation
- 11,578 built, V-Spec II Nür rarity and the $1,357,000 record sale
- The 25-year rule: when the R34 becomes legal in America

CHAPTERS
0:00 Banned in America
0:23 Where the GT-R began: the Hakosuka
0:55 The R32 and the Godzilla nickname
1:23 The R34 is revealed
1:39 The RB26DETT engine
2:06 A computer on wheels
2:30 Why Americans couldn't buy one
2:50 Rarity and the $1.357M auction
3:14 Godzilla comes to America

Watch all the full JDM Legends episodes: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLFjsSKQYu7HY
More 60-second car secrets: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLRQQ66l4AD8Q

QUICK ANSWERS
Is the R34 GT-R legal in the US? Under the 25-year rule, each R34 becomes eligible for import 25 years after its build month. The first cars (early 1999 builds) became eligible in 2024, and production ran to 2002.
How many R34 GT-Rs were made? 11,578 (1999-2002).
What engine does the R34 GT-R have? The RB26DETT 2.6-liter twin-turbo inline-six.
Why is the GT-R called Godzilla? Australia's Wheels magazine nicknamed the R32 GT-R "Godzilla", the monster from Japan.
